name: authoring.slide
description: Per-slide checks while a deck is being built (HTML or PPTX). One slide at a time, from its title, body text, notes and whether it carries a figure. Produces: ship / revise / escalate per slide. Traces of what the author did next (shortened, split, added a figure, shipped) become implied labels for these questions (extract/trace-implied.ts). Drafted 2026-09-25 for the wiring batch.

modules.name: slide-craft
modules.purpose: Whether one slide carries one claim, reads at a glance, and does not lean on the speaker.

oneClaimHeadline.instructions: Does the title state a claim, rather than name a topic?

criteria.true: The title is a sentence someone could agree or disagree with.
criteria.false: The title is a label such as a noun phrase, a section name or a question.

bodyRepeatsTitle.instructions: Does the body text restate the title without adding anything to it?

criteria.true: The body says the same thing as the title in other words.
criteria.false: The body adds evidence, an example, a step or a detail the title does not contain.

readableAtAGlance.instructions: Can the body text be read in a single glance while someone is speaking?

criteria.true: A few short lines; nothing has to be studied.
criteria.false: Paragraphs, nested lists or dense sentences that need reading time.

needsSpeakerToMakeSense.instructions: Would a reader who sees only this slide, without the notes, be unable to tell what it is saying?

criteria.true: The slide alone leaves the point unclear; the notes carry it.
criteria.false: The point is clear from the slide alone.

slideRole.instructions: What job does this slide do in the deck?

criteria.claim: States a point the deck is arguing.
criteria.evidence: Shows data, an example or a demonstration that supports a point.
criteria.agenda: Lists what is coming or where the audience is.
criteria.transition: Marks a change of part with little content.
criteria.ask: Requests a decision, an action or a next step from the audience.

compose.positive: the slide can ship as it is

notForJev.judgement: Word, line and bullet counts, font size, overflow
notForJev.instead: code over the slide text and the render (extract/trace metrics)

notForJev.judgement: Does the deck order argue, and is one accent used per deck?
notForJev.instead: needs the whole deck; code over the sequence for accents, a text model for the argument
token check and WCAG contrast in code
a named human (C10); the trace records the decision
